title: Danish pharma giant Novo to use Anthropic's Claude to advance AI drug discovery
content:
The deal underscores a broader push by drugmakers to integrate AI across research and development to boost new drug discovery.
Novo, previously Novo Nordisk, the Danish pharmaceutical company behind Ozempic, has partnered with Anthropic to accelerate the development of new medicines using artificial intelligence.
“Joining forces with Anthropic will supercharge our R&D organisation and help us on our mission to bring new, transformative health solutions to people living with chronic diseases,“ said Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo, in a press release Wednesday.
The pharmaceutical giant will use Anthropic’s models and Claude Science to advance scientific reasoning for Research and Development (R&D), the company announced.
Beyond increasing productivity in R&D, Novo’s CEO said AI tools can offer “completely new scientific opportunities” and help reasoning and understanding of human biology and drug mechanics.
"AI’s increasing capability brings with it the potential to compress a century’s worth of biological and medical breakthroughs into a decade," said Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO of Anthropic.
He added that by giving leading researchers access to safe, capable, and trusted frontier models, it is possible to shorten research timelines, improve outcomes, and discover medicines and treatments that significantly improve human life.
This partnership comes amid Novo’s bet on AI to fast-track drug research. The pharma giant is already using OpenAI’s science GPT-Rosalind, after sealing the deal in April to use advanced AI to analyse complex datasets, identify potential drugs, and cut the time between research and patient access.
In 2024, the Novo Nordisk Foundation partnered with Nvidia and the Export and Investment Fund of Denmark (EIFO) to establish the Danish Centre for AI Innovation, which operates Gefion – Denmark's first AI-ready supercomputer.
Anthropic is also expanding its work in the life sciences sector. In May 2026, the tech company announced a collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb to deploy Claude across the company's research, clinical development, manufacturing, commercial, and corporate functions.

report.summary: Novo partners with Anthropic to deploy Claude and Claude Science across drug discovery R&D, expanding pharma's push to integrate AI into medicine development.
report.background: Drug discovery traditionally takes 10-15 years and billions of dollars, with high failure rates, so pharma companies are turning to AI to shorten timelines from target identification to clinical trials. Novo, the Danish maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, faces pressure to diversify beyond its GLP-1 franchise. It already signed with OpenAI in April to use GPT-Rosalind for analysing complex datasets and identifying drug candidates. In 2024, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Nvidia, and Denmark's EIFO established the Danish Centre for AI Innovation, which operates the Gefion supercomputer. Anthropic is also expanding in life sciences after a May 2026 collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb. The deal reflects a broader race among AI labs to serve regulated, high-value scientific sectors.
key_points: Novo will use Anthropic's frontier models and Claude Science to advance scientific reasoning in R&D, targeting chronic diseases. CEO Mike Doustdar said the partnership will 'supercharge' Novo's R&D organisation and unlock 'completely new scientific opportunities' in understanding human biology and drug mechanisms.

Novo is pursuing a multi-vendor AI strategy: it already uses OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind under an April deal to analyse datasets, identify potential drugs, and cut time between research and patient access. Working with both OpenAI and Anthropic reduces single-supplier dependency in a critical function.

Anthropic is deepening its life-sciences push. After a May 2026 collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb spanning research, clinical development, manufacturing, and commercial functions, the Novo deal adds another major pharma client to Anthropic's enterprise portfolio.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei framed the ambition dramatically, saying AI could 'compress a century's worth of biological and medical breakthroughs into a decade' by giving researchers safe, capable frontier models that shorten timelines and improve outcomes.

Denmark's AI infrastructure supports the deal: the Danish Centre for AI Innovation, backed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, Nvidia, and EIFO, runs Gefion, the country's first AI-ready supercomputer, giving Novo a domestic compute and research ecosystem.
report.impact: For the AI industry, the deal validates frontier LLMs as scientific instruments and strengthens Anthropic's enterprise life-sciences business, intensifying rivalry with OpenAI for pharma R&D budgets. For developers, it signals growing demand for scientific agents, domain-specific evals, reproducible workflows, and secure data handling, plus hybrid systems that combine LLMs with tools like protein-structure predictors and cheminformatics libraries. For regular users, the promise is faster, cheaper drug development and new treatments for chronic diseases, but clinical trials, regulatory review, and biology's complexity mean benefits will arrive gradually rather than overnight. Privacy, bias, and hype risks will require careful oversight.
report.tools: Follow Anthropic's Claude Science and Claude Developer Platform APIs, plus MCP connectors for lab and data tools. Open-source options include AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, OpenFold, and Chai-1 for structure prediction; RDKit, DeepChem, and Nvidia BioNeMo for molecular modelling; and Open Targets, ChEMBL, and the Protein Data Bank for training data. These help developers prototype AI-driven discovery workflows similar to those Novo may deploy.
